docs.title: vergil-fixture-rust-lib
docs.text:
A test fixture, not a real library

This crate is a Vergil test fixture. It has no users, and it is never published to crates.io.

vergil-fixture-rust-lib is a small Rust library that exists so Vergil's Rust support has a real crate to work on. Each fixture run makes a small change to it and drives that change through Vergil's whole cycle for real: the PR, CI, the merge, the release and this docs site. A step that breaks shows up here before it reaches a real Rust repo.

It exercises:

  • vrg-validate for Rust: cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo check, the tests under cargo llvm-cov at 100% line coverage, and the cargo deny audit against Vergil's packaged license and advisory policy;
  • the CI and release workflows a real Rust library gets, with every fleet automation enabled;
  • three real runtime dependencies, serde, serde_json and thiserror, so the audit, the license check and Dependabot have real work to do.

Why the fixtures exist, and how a fixture run works, is set out in the language fixture repos spec.

docs.title: API
docs.text: Everything public is re-exported from the crate root, vergil_fixture_rust_lib.

docs.title: greet
docs.text:
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String

Greets name, trimmed of surrounding whitespace. A blank name greets the world.

use vergil_fixture_rust_lib::greet;

assert_eq!(greet("Ada"), "Hello, Ada");
assert_eq!(greet("  Grace "), "Hello, Grace");
assert_eq!(greet(""), "Hello, world");

docs.title: parse_greeting and Greeting
docs.text:
pub fn parse_greeting(json: &str) -> Result<Greeting, Error>

pub struct Greeting {
    pub name: String,
    pub punctuation: Option<String>,
}

impl Greeting {
    pub fn render(&self) -> String
}

parse_greeting reads a greeting from a JSON object with a required name and an optional punctuation, and trims the name. Greeting also serializes back to the same JSON with serde_json. render gives the greeting as text.

use vergil_fixture_rust_lib::parse_greeting;

let greeting = parse_greeting(r#"{"name": "Ada", "punctuation": "!"}"#)?;
assert_eq!(greeting.render(), "Hello, Ada!");

It fails with:

  • Error::Json when the input is not JSON, has no name, or has a field other than name and punctuation;
  • Error::BlankName when the name is empty or only whitespace.

docs.title: word_count
docs.text:
pub fn word_count(text: &str) -> usize

Counts the whitespace-separated words in text.

use vergil_fixture_rust_lib::word_count;

assert_eq!(word_count("the quick  brown fox"), 4);
assert_eq!(word_count(""), 0);

docs.title: initials
docs.text:
pub fn initials(text: &str) -> String

The upper-cased first letter of each whitespace-separated word in text.

use vergil_fixture_rust_lib::initials;

assert_eq!(initials("Ada Lovelace"), "AL");
assert_eq!(initials("émilie du châtelet"), "ÉDC");

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
pub enum Error {
    Json(serde_json::Error),
    BlankName,
}

The error from the library's fallible functions. It implements std::error::Error; for Error::Json the source is the serde_json error.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: The crate is not on crates.io (a fixture never reaches a package registry), so work on it from a clone of the repository.

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
Validation runs in Vergil's Rust dev image, the same way CI runs it:

vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate

That formats, lints, type-checks, tests at 100% line coverage and audits the dependencies. There is no other validation command.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: Path What it holds src/lib.rs The crate root: its modules and the pub use lines that make up the public API src/greeting.rs The greeting functions src/text.rs The text functions src/error.rs The library's error type tests/ One integration-test file per module

docs.title: Adding a function
docs.text:
Each fixture run adds one function, without restructuring the crate:

  1. Write its tests in the tests/ file for its theme, or a new one.
  2. Add the function, with a doc comment, to the module for its theme, or to a new module declared in src/lib.rs.
  3. Add it to the pub use lines in src/lib.rs.
  4. Document it on the API page.
  5. Run vrg-container-run -- vrg-validate.
